entry.title: Dynamics of the Liquidity Profile in Concentrated Liquidity Provision: An SPIDE Approach
entry.summary: We model the dynamics of the liquidity profile in Uniswap~V3 and other concentrated-liquidity automated market makers with a stochastic partial integro-differential equation (SPIDE). The profile, the aggregate of all provider positions across tick space, evolves under a degenerate Sturm--Liouville operator, which encodes mean-reverting concentration around the market price, coupled with a Hilbert--Schmidt integral operator, which captures nonlocal redistribution driven by provider repositioning. We establish existence and uniqueness of the mild solution in a weighted $L^2$ space built on the Gegenbauer eigensystem, and reduce the SPIDE to a coupled system of linear stochastic differential equations whose low-order modes describe the level, slope, and curvature of the profile. Pairing the SPIDE with a log-price process yields tractable expressions for pool reserves, pool value, and loss-versus-rebalancing under Ornstein--Uhlenbeck-type and Black--Scholes-type noise. A finite-rank calibration in a fixed reference frame, applied to three Uniswap pools, gives interpretable estimates and lowers active-band forecast error relative to a martingale benchmark on the two pools compatible with the stationary specification. On the third pool, out-of-sample diagnostics are consistent with nonstationarity, which motivates price-aware and time-varying extensions.

entry.title: Nonexistence of Strongly Regular Graphs via Gegenbauer Positivity and SRG Counting
entry.summary: This paper develops a natural extension of the multipoint spherical semidefinite method of Liao and Yu~\cite{LY}, studying the interaction between semidefinite programming and strongly regular graph counting. Starting from the positive semidefinite kernels furnished by Gegenbauer polynomials, we express weighted kernel sums and counting identities in the same labelled induced-subgraph counts. Eliminating the counting equations gives a semidefinite feasibility problem. Numerical dual solutions guide the construction of rational certificates, whose contradiction identities are verified exactly. Our aim is a systematic method that treats many parameter sets through the same construction. For least eigenvalue $-3$, it gives new counting certificates for $(351,140,73,44)$, $(550,162,75,36)$, $(703,182,81,35)$ and $(1344,221,88,26)$, previously excluded by Liao and Yu~\cite[Theorem~1]{LY}, and for six additional parameter sets: \[ \begin{array}{@{}lll@{}} (375,102,45,21), & (405,132,63,33), & (441,88,35,13),\\ (476,133,60,28), & (540,147,66,30), & (575,112,45,16). \end{array} \] Seven certificates use Gegenbauer positivity and counting information alone at the displayed orders. The cases $v=375,441,575$ additionally use proved short-vector restrictions, unique vertex extensions, and integer common-neighbour inequalities. The proofs end in displayed inequalities with incompatible signs. Their justification is given by the dual identities and the proved positivity and counting relations; accompanying code automates the longer rational arithmetic.

entry.title: Continuous Narayana Interpolations: Hankel Total Positivity and Log-Convexity Preservation
entry.summary: We study a continuous interpolation between the type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana triangles. Using a direct Gegenbauer-moment proof and a continuant comparison criterion, we show that the row polynomials form a coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive sequence for every real $θ\ge0$, and establish the same property for the moment sequences associated with all tails of the corresponding Jacobi matrix. Their $γ$-expansion, real-rootedness and Stieltjes moment representation are explicit, as are the exact orders of vanishing and extreme coefficients of arbitrary Hankel minors. This confirms and strengthens Rodelet--Causse--Tevlin's log-convexity conjecture for super Narayana polynomials. We further extend Wang--Yang's total positivity of the type~$A$ and $B$ Narayana triangles and strict total positivity of the associated squares to every real $θ>-1$, using Pólya-frequency sequences and a gamma-product moment representation. We also prove that the continuous Narayana transformations preserve strong $t$-log-convexity for every $θ\ge0$, and that every $d$-Hoggatt transformation has the same property for integers $d\ge1$. The preservation proofs employ the Zhu--Sun criterion and a mixed-minor one-sign-change argument based on a hypergeometric hitting-probability inequality.

entry.title: A Proof of the Koumandos--Ruscheweyh Conjecture
entry.summary: We prove the Koumandos--Ruscheweyh conjecture for every $0<ρ\leq1$. If $ν(ρ)$ is the unique root in $(0,1]$ of $\int_0^{(1+ρ)π}t^{μ-1}\sin(t-ρπ)\,\mathrm{d}t=0$, then $(1-z)^ρs_n^μ(z)\prec((1+z)/(1-z))^ρ$ for every $n\geq0$, $0<μ\leqν(ρ)$ and $z\in\mathbb{D}$, where $s_n^μ(z)=\sum_{k=0}^n(μ)_kz^k/k!$. The parameter $ν(ρ)$ is optimal. The proof combines an all-parameter gamma-coefficient comparison with an exact beta integral and a binomial variance estimate, reducing the infinitely many degrees to finitely many continuous interval inequalities. The remaining inequalities are certified by 256-bit ball arithmetic; rational covers, source code and alternative-formula verifiers are provided. The weak positive-real-part conjecture follows as a sharp corollary. We also derive sharp consequences for starlike functions and Gegenbauer polynomial sections: a full-parameter convolution subordination, the optimal starlike order for uniform partial-sum sectors, and the optimal Gegenbauer parameter and sector angle. The necessary bounds and angular sharpness are obtained from explicit kernels and interior scaling limits.

entry.title: Half-ladder partial waves for all $n,d$ with applications to string theory
entry.summary: Given any four-point scattering amplitude, the partial wave expansion resolves its residues into contributions from individual spin-$s$ internal particles, where each coefficient in the expansion must be non-negative due to unitarity. In this paper, we introduce a partial wave expansion tailored to "half-ladder" Feynman diagrams at generic multiplicity $n$ and spacetime dimension $d$, with scalars on the external lines and massive bosons on the internal lines. Derived by enforcing that the half-ladder residue is an eigenvector of each internal particle's angular momentum, each basis element is written as a sum over products of special functions related to the Gegenbauer polynomials, and we give a set of simple graphical rules for explicitly building any of them at generic $n$ and $d$. To put the formalism into action, we apply our technology to deformed "string theory" amplitudes, defined a priori in any dimension and with arbitrary Regge intercept $α_0$. By constructing multi-particle positivity tests for the half-ladder and "twisted" half-ladder diagrams, we show that the only amplitudes consistent with unitarity are those belonging to open bosonic string theory ($α_0 = -1$) below the critical dimension $d \leq 26$. In particular, we confirm the expectation that $Z$-theory ($α_0 = 0$) fails to define a unitary string theory at finite $α'$. Finally, for the open bosonic string, we show how knowledge of the partial wave expansion allows us to resolve the contributions to the half-ladder diagram from individual degenerate states at a given level and spin in a purely on-shell analysis. As an ancillary file, we include a Python script combwaves.py which implements the partial wave expansion given a generic (twisted) half-ladder residue.
